record.paper_title: Open problems in renewal, coupling and Palm theory
record.original_question: Let Q(X, ξ) be an invariant preserving G × G kernel associated with a pair (X, ξ), and recall that Theorem 4.4 characterizes mass-stationarity by requiring equation (4.2) to hold for all bounded invariant preserving kernels Q(X, ξ). Does the same characterization remain valid if one restricts attention to kernels Q(X, ξ) that are Markovian, meaning that each Q(X, ξ)(s, ·) has total mass one?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.2 Does Theorem 4.4 hold if the kernels Q(X,ξ) are restricted to be Markovian?

If Q(X,ξ) is not only bounded but has total mass one [is Markovian] then we can introduce a random element T in G with conditional distribution Q(X,ξ)(0,·) given (X,ξ) and write (4.2) on the probabilistic form (4.1).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a locally compact second countable topological group with Haar measure $\lambda$, and let $(X,\xi)$ be a pair consisting of a random element $X$ and a random measure $\xi$ on $G$ defined on a probability space. A kernel $Q(X,\xi)(s,\cdot)$ from $G$ to $G$ (depending measurably on $(X,\xi)$) is called an invariant preserving $G\times G$ kernel for $(X,\xi)$ if it is bounded and satisfies the appropriate $G$-invariance and $\xi$-preserving properties (so that integrating $Q$ against $\xi$ produces an invariant balance with respect to the group action).

Recall the following characterization of mass-stationarity: the pair $(X,\xi)$ is mass-stationary if and only if the identity
$$\mathbb{E}\!\int\!\!\int f(\theta_s X,\theta_s \xi,-s)\,Q(X,\xi)(0,ds)\,\xi(d\cdot) \;=\; \mathbb{E}\!\int\!\!\int f(X,\xi,s)\,Q(X,\xi)(\cdot,ds)\,\xi(d\cdot) \qquad (\ast)$$
holds for every bounded measurable function $f$ and every bounded invariant preserving $G\times G$ kernel $Q(X,\xi)$.

A kernel $Q(X,\xi)$ is called Markovian if $Q(X,\xi)(s,G)=1$ for every $s\in G$ (almost surely).

Question: Does the above characterization of mass-stationarity remain valid if the class of test kernels in $(\ast)$ is restricted to those invariant preserving $G\times G$ kernels $Q(X,\xi)$ that are Markovian?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up a definitive resolution of whether mass-stationarity can be characterized using only Markovian invariant-preserving kernels. The characterization via general bounded invariant preserving kernels appears in works of Last and Thorisson on Palm pairs and mass-stationarity, but I found no later paper announcing a positive or negative answer to the Markovian-restriction version. Status appears unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Construction and characterization of stationary and mass-stationary random measures on R^d
status_evidence.snippet: Mass-stationarity ... intrinsic characterization of Palm versions with respect to stationary random measures.
status_evidence.claim: Mass-stationarity is studied via invariance under classes of invariant-preserving transport kernels, but no Markovian-only characterization is established.

status_evidence.title: Palm pairs and the general mass-transport principle
status_evidence.snippet: Q is mass-stationary for ξ iff it is invariant under bounded ξ-preserving invariant weighted transport-kernels.
status_evidence.claim: The known characterization uses bounded invariant ξ-preserving kernels; the Markovian restriction is not addressed.
